Hi all — pulled together three scenario sketches based on the forecast and some conservative operational assumptions. Attaching capacity_workbook_NorthStar.xlsx (tabbed by region & scenario). Summary here: 

1) Conservative (safety-first)- APAC: 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs (6 nodes @ 4 gpus/node)- EU: 12 x A100-equivalent GPUs (3 nodes)- US: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (2 nodes)
Notes: heavy reliance on cross-region burst lanes; slower rollout cadence; minimal burst buffer (10% over baseline).

2) Baseline (recommended for initial commitment)- APAC: 48 x A100-equiv (12 nodes)- EU: 24 x A100-equiv (6 nodes)- US: 12 x A100-equiv (3 nodes)
Notes: supports steady-state traffic for Q3 rollouts with 20-25% headroom; KV cache sized for 256 tokens, moderate batching.

3) Aggressive (growth-protect)- APAC: 80 x A100-equiv (20 nodes)- EU: 40 x A100-equiv (10 nodes)- US: 20 x A100-equiv (5 nodes)
Notes: built to avoid throttling during 2x traffic spikes; higher cost but minimal fallback risk.

Operational considerations and fallback matrix:
- Canary plan: provision 2-node canary in APAC (8 GPUs) + traffic split of 5-10% for 72 hours; roll to baseline if no errors and latency delta < 15%.
- Fallback lanes: enable model-variant fallback (quantized variant) in EU/US when regional latency or capacity breaches threshold; routing policy set to degrade to functionally equivalent smaller model.
- Node tiling recommendation: 4 gpus/node gives best packing for image+text workloads; if customer wants fractional cores we can propose fractional instances but it increases ops complexity.

Costs: workbook has a basic cost sheet with approximate monthly committed costs for each scenario (ballpark USD). I’ll update numbers if NorthStar confirms preferred activation cadence and SLOs.

Attachments: capacity_workbook_NorthStar.xlsx

Ben Carter
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

- Traffic split: APAC 60% / EU 25% / US 15% across peak windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency target = 220ms for APAC, 300ms EU, 320ms US.
- Sequence length: 128 tokens for our main flows (not 256). That should reduce cache pressure modestly.
- Activation order: we want APAC full baseline by 2027-06-01, EU canary + 1-week ramp starting 2027-06-08, US can be held for Q3 unless traffic grows earlier.
- Procurement timeline: internal approval by 2027-05-30, legal needs SOW + cost by 2027-05-24.

Can you provide a canary-run checklist and a short paragraph on fallback behavior we can paste into the packet? Also, please include the monthly committed cost delta between baseline and aggressive (rounded).

If you can get an updated workbook + SOW draft references over the next week that would be great.

— Alice
